text: When designing REST APIs, it is important to follow some best practices to make your API easy to use and maintain. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success and 404 when something is not found. Third, write good documentation so that other developers can understand how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these simple rules will help you build reliable and professional APIs.
